body: - G-Py-7 (wrap external CLIs as typed functions over the injected Runner) is deviated by the changed line in `push_current_branch`:

- This inlines a mutating `git push` argv and checks `result.returncode` ad hoc, when the codebase already ships a typed wrapper that produces the byte-identical argv: `git.push_set_upstream(runner, remote, refspec, *, cwd=None)` in `python/larch/git/git.py`, defined as `_run(runner, ["git", "push", "-u", remote, refspec], cwd=cwd)`. The sibling push path `push_branch` in the same file (`python/larch/git/push.py`) already routes through that wrapper — `git.push_set_upstream(runner, remote, "HEAD", cwd=cwd)` with `remote == "origin"` — so `push_current_branch` is now the lone push site that reaches past the wrapper for the exact argv the wrapper exists to produce. The fix is a drop-in: `result = git.push_set_upstream(runner, "origin", "HEAD", cwd=cwd)`, which converges both push entry points on the typed seam and removes the hardcoded literal. Note the regression test added in `python/tests/git/test_push.py` is unaffected either way, since it only asserts the resolved argv shape.

- Note (no identifier cited, as it is a class-alignment strength rather than a breach): the change does fix the one inconsistent push instance — the in-file sibling `push_branch` was already correct via `push_set_upstream` — so the fix-discipline expectation to converge the class is met on the primary sibling; the only residual is the wrapper-bypass above.
